subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw core accept first-class per-agent browser-profile binding with per-profile proxy support, and if so what config and inheritance contract should be public?
rationale: The request adds new public config/API surface and changes browser network egress plus session isolation boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Design In Browser Plugin
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella for a maintainer-approved browser-plugin/core config design covering proxy secrets, SSRF policy, agent defaults, subagent inheritance, and diagnostics.

options.title: Split Remaining Work
options.body: Use the broader proxy issue and the subagent browser-session issue as separate canonical tracks, then close this issue only after maintainers intentionally split the scope.

options.title: External Orchestration Only
options.body: Document remote CDP, node browser proxy, and external browser-lock style approaches as the supported pattern without adding new core config.

recommendation.title: Design In Browser Plugin
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella for a maintainer-approved browser-plugin/core config design covering proxy secrets, SSRF policy, agent defaults, subagent inheritance, and diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent browser plugin boundary and SDK-seam history makes Peter the best available routing candidate for this product/API decision.
